subject: function:ProcessEffects
value: WHEN THE TARGET COMPUTES A VALUE ONCE AND YOUR SOURCE SPELLS THE SUBEXPRESSION TWICE, THE DIFFERENCE IS SOURCE-REACHABLE AND SHOWS UP AS A WHOLE MISSING STACK SLOT PLUS A SCHEDULE THAT LOOKS LIKE ALLOCATOR NOISE. Two distinct tells, both MEASURED on ProcessEffects, both closed by introducing a plain named local. TELL 1 -- `stfs SLOT(r1)` IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWED BY `lfs` FROM THE SAME SLOT is not a redundant round trip: it is a named f32 local whose live range crosses a CALL while every callee-saved FPR is already holding a hoisted constant, so it MUST be memory-homed. Target stored `radius + player->radius` to slot 332 and reloaded it at both uses; we recomputed the `fadds` at the second use and therefore never allocated the slot at all. Writing `f32 sumr = radius + player->radius;` and using `sumr` at both sites took real 1608 -> 1592, insns 2301 -> 2303 (toward target 2309), multiset 20t -> 16t, and restored the slot COUNT to exactly 79/79. TELL 2 -- the same construct's other half: the target computed a dot product BEFORE a conditional it does not depend on, ours computed it after the join. This reads as a scheduler difference and is not one; naming the value (`f32 dp = delta[0]*dir[0] + delta[2]*dir[2];` placed before the `if`) let MWCC schedule it exactly where target does. Applied at the THREE sibling scan loops (player/enemy/item), it took real 1592 -> 1518 and fuzzy 94.4101 -> 95.9415 with NO change to insn count or multiset -- i.e. the coarse structural metrics were completely blind to it. THE PROCEDURE: when a `--ops` cluster shows the same opcodes on both sides in a different ORDER around a branch, or a slotdiff row shows a TARGET-ONLY slot whose uses are `1 store + N loads`, grep the source for the expression the target loaded and check whether you spelled it more than once. CRITICAL ALIGNMENT COROLLARY: this exact axis (`sum = radius + player->radius` as a local) was probed a run earlier, measured real 2317 = REGRESSED, and parked with the honest note "target homes it in a STACK SLOT 332(r1), ours colors an FPR - slot-homing lever unknown". The lever was never a source form -- it was FPR PRESSURE, and the park only fell after unrelated prologue work filled the callee-saved FPRs the way target fills them. A park on a pressure-dependent axis is a statement about the surrounding allocation, not about the form; re-probe it after ANY change to the constant-hoist block.
